A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, controlled SFT/RL training experiments, PCA measurements and token-distribution analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds Qwen3-8B training ablations, gradient-norm analyses and response-length measurements.

M1.justification: The main UniReason training recipe remains unchanged. Section 5 adds procedural variants for ablation, including on-policy SFT using self-generated responses and off-policy RL using teacher-generated responses. These are limited training adaptations, without a new model architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 47K math and 232K General-Reasoner training collections and the same twelve evaluation benchmarks. The new ablations reuse the math queries and retained task coverage; they introduce model and training configurations rather than new domains or tasks.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparator roster is retained. v2 adds targeted on-policy/off-policy SFT and RL comparisons, including RL with and without KL regularization, in Tables 3–4. Qwen3-14B-think also joins the PCA comparison in Table 2.

E3.justification: Section 2.1 replaces the original relative-gain transferability metric with standard-deviation normalization, signed square-root transformation and difficulty weighting. Section 5 introduces a separate Qwen3-8B controlled design varying sampling policy, update weighting and KL regularization. The existing 14B training and benchmark evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 5 tests which training components explain transferability. Appendix A.5 adds gradient-norm trajectories and summaries, plus online SFT/RL response-length comparisons. These substantially extend the earlier PCA and token-shift diagnostics, which are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same ten-sample, three-sample and single-sample evaluation practices, without adding training-seed replication, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new TI normalization and temporal gradient variance characterize benchmark or training variation rather than estimation uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 adds ablation outcomes, gradient statistics and Qwen3-14B-think PCA scores. Reported UniReason RL TIother/TInon change from 79.6/29.3 to 82.3/52.2 under the revised metric. All 90 original per-benchmark result rows remain unchanged, so these TI changes do not establish improved model performance.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 substantially redefines TI through normalized absolute gains, signed square roots and weighted domain indices. New Section 5.1 formalizes a unified surrogate loss parameterized by sampling distribution, credit weights and KL regularization. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The broad RL-versus-SFT transfer claim remains. However, the introduction and conclusion add a substantive explanatory contribution: sampling distribution is identified as the principal factor, credit assignment and negative updates help, and KL regularization contributes comparatively little.

C2.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.5 add explanations involving reduced training/inference distribution mismatch, conservative updates, negative-example learning and exploration inferred from longer responses. They also interpret KL regularization as less influential because on-policy sampling already aligns updates with the model distribution.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 adds ablation construction details, including eight teacher responses per query and highest-reward response selection. Core 14B hyperparameters are retained. Conversely, v2 removes the project code/model access links and the pooled top-250-token selection detail for the unchanged word clouds.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work positioning are retained. Citation ordering, expanded author names and the replacement DeepScaler reference URL are bibliographic changes rather than additions to the research context.

P1.justification: Existing discussion, especially Section 4 and the conclusion, is selectively condensed. Related work becomes Section 5.3, appendices are reorganized, an LLM-use disclosure and future-work paragraph are added, and author contributions and acknowledgments are removed. Most existing exposition remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The document adopts a different template, typography and page layout. Figure 2 is redrawn with linear rather than signed-logarithmic TI values. Three tables and three figures are added, while the original token case-study table and position-wise rank-shift figure move from the main text to the appendix.

improvement.justification: The new component ablations and training diagnostics strengthen v1's explanations. However, the revised TI formula does not reproduce Table 1's RL TInon: the printed inputs yield about 84.1, versus 52.2 reported. Table 3 also conflicts with Section 5.2 about off-policy RL's KL setting, and project access links disappear. These competing gains and reporting problems prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
